outcome: Improve order promise, routing, delivery exceptions, returns and refunds across stores, warehouses and carriers.
overview: Omnichannel promises break where systems meet: stock that is accurate in the warehouse but not on the shop floor, carrier events that arrive too late, and returns that sit uncredited while the customer chases a refund. This solution assembles authoritative availability across stores, warehouses and carriers, then routes each order to the fulfilment option that meets the promise at the lowest total cost, flags delivery risk early and offers operators approved recovery actions. Returns and refunds follow policy limits with idempotent posting so nothing is credited twice. An 8–12 week lane or category proof of value measures on-time-in-full, cost per order and refund cycle time against an agreed baseline.

benefits.text: Improve on-time-in-full delivery and reduce split shipments on the pilot lanes
benefits.source: Redington Retail catalogue; consistent with published order-management benchmark ranges
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Effect size to validate against the customer’s own lane and carrier performance during the PoV — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce cost per order and cost per return by routing on total cost rather than default rules
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on inventory accuracy and on carrier and store handling costs being available at the granularity the router needs

benefits.text: Shorten refund cycle time and give customers a transparent, current order status
benefits.source: Reference design — policy-limited refund automation with idempotent posting and customer communication
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Bounded by payment-provider settlement times and by the customer’s own refund policy and approval limits

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); order, customer and payment references remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No authoritative, near-real-time stock position across stores and warehouses
notFor.why: Routing on stale availability produces confident promises the network cannot keep, which is worse than no promise at all

notFor.situation: No documented returns, refund and remedy policy with stated approval limits
notFor.why: The design executes policy; where the policy is informal, automation would encode whatever the last operator happened to do

notFor.situation: Carriers cannot provide event data or accept booking requests through an interface
notFor.why: Early exception detection and recovery both depend on carrier events arriving in time to act on them

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns fulfilment policy, carrier and payment contracts and every exception approval · Duration: 8–12 weeks PoV; further 16–28 weeks to network scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, orchestration engineer, integration engineer; customer fulfilment owner, store operations lead, customer-service lead, payments owner, finance reconciler · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery, stock-accuracy review and cost baseline
2) Event backbone and authoritative availability build
3) Promise, routing and returns policy configuration
4) Operator workbench, reconciliation and failure testing
5) Controlled lane or category go-live with daily review
6) Benefit review and handover
deliverables: Order, inventory and payment records reconcile end to end with no orphaned transactions
SLA and cost-per-order thresholds met on the pilot lanes
Replay and idempotency tests pass — no duplicate refunds under retry
Carrier-failure drill completed with the degraded-mode procedure exercised
Customer status transparency verified across channels and operations UAT completed
effort: 8–12 weeks PoV; further 16–28 weeks to network scale
languages: English delivery; Arabic and English customer order communications supported
